$comment: Authored content for FORM-A's items. Committed as DATA so a reviewer can read what was written without reading a script. Distractor rationales name the specific misconception each wrong choice catches; a distractor written only to be wrong is noise. Spanish is authored here and marked needs-review — it has not been checked by a certified translator.
authoredBy: Claude Opus 5 · pilot for US.46 / US.60 / US.23

q-us44-dok1-2.explanation: The RFC was Hoover's main federal intervention: it lent public money to banks, railroads and large firms on the theory that keeping big institutions solvent would stop failures cascading down to workers. That 'top-down' logic is why the RFC is the standard contrast with the New Deal's direct relief.
q-us44-dok1-2.dokRationale: The student retrieves what one named agency did. No relationship or inference is required, which is DOK-1; asking why the RFC's design drew criticism would be DOK-2.

A: Raising tariffs was the Hawley-Smoot Tariff of 1930, a separate Hoover-era policy that restricted trade rather than lending money.
confuses the RFC with the Hawley-Smoot Tariff
C: This describes the failure of Hoover's voluntary-cooperation approach, in which he asked business to hold wages. The RFC was the opposite: a funded federal lender.
confuses the RFC with Hoover's voluntary cooperation policy
D: This is the Bonus Army episode of 1932, a protest by WWI veterans. It is an event, not an agency, and had no lending function.
confuses the RFC with the Bonus Army episode

q-us44-dok2-1.dokRationale: The student recalls who the marchers were and what Hoover did. Both halves are retrieved facts, which is DOK-1; explaining how the episode shifted public opinion toward FDR would be DOK-2.

A: This is the Reconstruction Finance Corporation, a lending agency, not a protest.
confuses the Bonus Army with the RFC
B: This is the Hawley-Smoot Tariff, a trade policy unrelated to the veterans' march.
confuses the Bonus Army with the Hawley-Smoot Tariff
C: This describes why Hoover's voluntary wage-maintenance appeals failed, not the veterans' bonus demand.
confuses the Bonus Army with Hoover's voluntary cooperation policy

PSTIM-0149.dokRationale: The student must read an image of infrastructure and infer what it shows about the federal government's role — a relationship between evidence and a claim, which is DOK-2. Naming the agency in the photograph would be DOK-1.

B: The TVA is the clearest case of the opposite: the federal government built and ran dams and sold the power itself.
reverses the direction of federal involvement under the New Deal
C: The TVA was created by Congress in 1933 as a federally owned corporation. Reading it as private misses why critics called it socialism.
mistakes a federally owned corporation for a private company
D: Federal public works on this scale had no 1920s precedent; that discontinuity is the point of the image.
treats the New Deal as continuous with 1920s policy

U5-DOK2-0027.dokRationale: The student must connect features of New Deal programs to the political charge made against them, which is a cause-and-claim relationship — DOK-2. Recalling that critics used the word 'socialism' would be DOK-1.
U5-DOK2-0027.stemEs: ¿Por qué los críticos del New Deal afirmaban que los programas de FDR representaban socialismo?
U5-DOK2-0027.explanationEs: El New Deal amplió enormemente la función del gobierno federal: reguló la industria y la agricultura, creó empleo público y estableció la Seguridad Social. Los críticos consideraron que esa expansión era socialismo, aunque la propiedad privada y los mercados siguieron intactos.

B: FDR never proposed nationalising major industries. The charge rested on regulation and public employment, not government ownership.
overstates the charge as nationalisation of industry
C: Private property rights were not abolished; New Deal farm policy paid owners to limit production rather than redistributing their land.
confuses regulation and subsidy with land redistribution
D: Private and religious charities continued throughout the 1930s; federal relief supplemented them because their resources had been exhausted.
assumes federal relief replaced private charity

PSTIM-0130.dokRationale: The student matches a described deployment to the named policy that explains it. This is retrieval of a labelled concept — DOK-1.

A: Détente was the 1970s easing of tensions under Nixon, two decades after Korea and opposite in posture.
places a 1970s policy in a 1950 context
B: Isolationism is the refusal to intervene abroad. Sending troops to Korea is its contradiction.
reverses the policy the deployment demonstrates
D: Imperialism means acquiring territory. The stated aim in Korea was to hold a line, not to annex it.
confuses containing an opponent with acquiring territory

U7-DOK1-0002.dokRationale: The student recalls which initiative a named speech announced. One retrieved association, which is DOK-1.

A: The Eisenhower Doctrine came a decade later, in 1957, and addressed the Middle East.
confuses the Marshall Plan with the Eisenhower Doctrine
B: NATO was a 1949 military alliance. The Marshall Plan was economic aid and came first.
confuses economic aid with the military alliance
C: The Berlin Airlift was a 1948-49 supply operation for one city, not a Europe-wide recovery programme.
confuses a single-city operation with a continental aid programme

PS-0090.dokRationale: The student must read a source and infer what it implies about the alliance's durability — drawing a conclusion from evidence, which is DOK-2. Naming the three Allies would be DOK-1.
PS-0090.stemEs: Lea el extracto a continuación y responda la pregunta. El extracto describe la Gran Alianza entre Estados Unidos, Gran Bretaña y la Unión Soviética.
PS-0090.explanationEs: El extracto afirma que la alianza se sostenía únicamente en un enemigo común. Esto implica que, al desaparecer ese enemigo, las diferencias ideológicas entre las democracias occidentales y la Unión Soviética quedarían al descubierto, lo que ocurrió al terminar la guerra.

A: The source points to ideology, not personalities. The three leaders in fact sustained working cooperation through the war.
substitutes personal friction for the structural cause the source names
B: The Allies did not share all military technology — the United States withheld the atomic programme from the Soviets entirely.
assumes full technology sharing among the Allies
C: The United Nations was designed to keep the Allies cooperating after 1945, and the blocs hardened afterward rather than before the war ended.
reverses the chronology of the UN and the Cold War blocs

PSTIM-0041.dokRationale: The student must interpret an image of a supply flight and infer the strategic message it sent — evidence to inference, which is DOK-2. Identifying the aircraft or the city would be DOK-1.

A: No Soviet troops were driven out. The airlift deliberately avoided force by flying over the blockade instead of breaking it.
reads a non-military response as a military one
B: Germany's division was not settled by a treaty during the airlift; the blockade ended in 1949 without one.
invents a negotiated settlement for the blockade
C: Sanctions were not the instrument, and Soviet communism continued for four more decades.
attributes the end of Soviet communism to a 1948 operation

PSTIM-0124.dokRationale: The student recalls which president is associated with building the canal. A single retrieved fact, which is DOK-1.

A: McKinley was president during the Spanish-American War and was assassinated in 1901, before canal construction began.
assigns the canal to the preceding administration
C: Wilson took office in 1913, the year before the canal opened; he did not initiate it.
credits the president in office at completion rather than construction
D: Taft succeeded Roosevelt and oversaw later construction, but the acquisition and decision were Roosevelt's.
credits Roosevelt's successor with the decision

STIM-0019.dokRationale: The cartoon's own labels name the territories on the menu, so the student recognises the subject rather than analysing an unstated argument. That recognition is DOK-1; asking what the cartoonist thought of expansion would be DOK-3.
STIM-0019.stemEs: Use la caricatura política para responder la pregunta. La caricatura de 1898 muestra al Tío Sam sentado a la mesa de un restaurante, mirando un menú que enumera territorios.
STIM-0019.explanationEs: El menú presenta los territorios como platos por elegir, lo que representa a Estados Unidos decidiendo qué territorios adquirir tras vencer a España en la Guerra Hispano-Estadounidense de 1898.

B: A refusal would be shown by pushing the menu away. Reading the menu is the act of choosing.
reverses what the menu imagery represents
C: The territories on the menu were annexed or occupied, not treated as independent trading partners.
recasts annexation as trade negotiation
D: The cartoon is dated after the fighting, and the menu lists territories rather than military options.
places the cartoon before the war rather than after

PS-0065.dokRationale: The student must interpret Roosevelt's boast and connect it to the actual sequence of events in Panama — inference from a source, which is DOK-2.
PS-0065.stemEs: Lea el extracto a continuación. Es una declaración del presidente Theodore Roosevelt sobre la Zona del Canal.
PS-0065.explanationEs: Cuando Colombia rechazó el tratado, Estados Unidos apoyó la revolución de Panamá en 1903 y de inmediato firmó un tratado con el nuevo país para obtener la Zona del Canal. La frase de Roosevelt reconoce que actuó primero y dejó el debate para después.

A: The French company sold its concession and equipment; the sovereignty dispute was with Colombia, not France.
substitutes France for Colombia as the aggrieved party
B: The United States built the canal itself with its own workforce rather than paying other nations to build it.
assumes the canal was contracted out to other nations
D: Panama declared independence from Colombia, not Spain; Spain had lost its mainland American colonies eighty years earlier.
confuses Colombia with Spain as the colonial power

PS-0067.dokRationale: The student must weigh the obstacles described in the source and identify which one the evidence supports as decisive — evaluating evidence for a claim, which is DOK-2.
PS-0067.stemEs: Lea el extracto a continuación. Describe la mano de obra empleada en la construcción del Canal de Panamá.
PS-0067.explanationEs: La fiebre amarilla y la malaria mataron a miles de trabajadores hasta que la campaña de control de mosquitos dirigida por William Gorgas redujo drásticamente las muertes. El control de la enfermedad, más que la ingeniería, fue lo que hizo posible terminar el canal.

A: The Chagres River was dammed rather than redirected, and it was one river, not four.
overstates the hydrological problem and its scale
B: There was no labour shortage: tens of thousands of Caribbean and European workers were recruited, which is what the source describes.
contradicts the source, which documents abundant recruited labour
C: Dynamite and steam shovels were used extensively; the Culebra Cut was blasted, not dug by hand.
assumes excavation was manual

q-us3-dok4-cr3.dokRationale: The student must construct and defend a claim using cited evidence from the source and outside knowledge. Building an argument rather than reporting one is DOK-3.

q-us6-dok4-cr3.dokRationale: The student must build an evidence-based argument and reason from it to a conclusion, which is DOK-3 rather than the retrieval or interpretation of DOK-1 and DOK-2.

q-us2-dok4-cr2.dokRationale: The student must weigh competing motives against evidence and argue a position, which requires strategic reasoning — DOK-3.
